input.text: Think about which list positions your summing loop visits. If you start at the second position, the very first number never gets added into the total, which explains why every output is short by exactly that first value (and why a single number produces zero).

content.text: Your loop is summing only part of the list. Double-check which index your loop starts at, and make sure the first number is included in the total.

input.text: The bug is an off-by-one in the loop bounds: range(1, len(nums)) starts at index 1, so nums[0] is never added to total. That is why "1 2 3" gives 2+3=5 and "7" gives 0. To sum every element, the loop must start at the first valid index, 0.
